'''Lawrence F. Dahl''' (June 2, 1929 – March 20, 2021) was an R.E. Rundle and Hilldale Professor of Chemistry at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]].<ref name="Grinnell">{{cite web|url=http://www.grinnell.edu/academic/noycevisit/fall2009/|title=Lawrence F. Dahl, Noyce Visiting Professor Ilia Guzei, Noyce Visiting Scholar|date=Fall 2009|publisher=Grinnell College|accessdate=January 19, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100527182215/http://www.grinnell.edu/academic/noycevisit/fall2009|archive-date=May 27, 2010|url-status=dead}}</ref> Dahl was an [[inorganic chemistry|inorganic chemist]], and his research focused on high-nuclearity metallic compounds.<ref name="chem">{{cite web|url=http://www.chem.wisc.edu/users/dahl|title=L. F. Dahl Faculty Page|date=September 17, 2003|publisher=Department of Chemistry, UW-Madison|accessdate=January 19, 2010|location=Madison, WI|archive-date=December 26, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181226024814/http://www.chem.wisc.edu/users/dahl|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was elected to the [[United States National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Sciences]] in 1988.<ref name="nytimes">{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1988/05/02/us/61-scientists-are-chosen-for-national-academy.html?pagewanted=1|title=61 Scientists Are Chosen For National Academy|date=May 2, 1988|work=The New York Times|pages=B7|accessdate=January 19, 2010}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Dahl was born in 1929. He earned his B.S. degree from the [[University of Louisville]] in 1951 and his Ph.D. from [[Iowa State University]] in 1956.<ref name="chem" />

==Career==
In 1957 Dahl joined the faculty in the chemistry department at the University of Wisconsin–Madison. His laboratory made significant contributions in the synthesis, structure, and bonding of [[transition metal]] compounds. Dahl trained 95 Ph.D. candidates, 24 M.S. students, 45 undergraduate research students, and 15 postdoctoral fellows.<ref name="Grinnell" />

==Selected awards and distinctions==
* 1969–1970 – [[Guggenheim Fellow]]<ref name="chem" />
* 1980 – Elected Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]<ref name="chem" />
* 1985 –  Alexander von Humboldt Award<ref name="Grinnell"/>
* 1988 – Elected to the National Academy of Sciences<ref name="nytimes" />
* 1992 – Elected Fellow of [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]<ref name="chem" />
* 1999 – [[Willard Gibbs Award]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://chicagoacs.org/content.php?page=Willard_Gibbs_Award|title=The Willard Gibbs Medal Founded by William A. Converse|date=January 1, 2014|publisher=American Chemical Society – Chicago Section|accessdate=April 29, 2015}}</ref>
* 2010 – [[F. Albert Cotton]] Award in Synthetic Inorganic Chemistry<ref name="ACS">{{cite web|url=http://portal.acs.org/portal/acs/corg/content?_nfpb=true&_pageLabel=PP_ARTICLEMAIN&node_id=1313&content_id=CNBP_022826&use_sec=true&sec_url_var=region1&__uuid=da510a5a-3de8-4ce4-bc2a-17f6c0afd95b|title=ACS 2010 National Award Winners|year=2010|publisher=American Chemical Society|accessdate=January 19, 2010}}</ref>
* 2014 – Elected Fellow of the American Crystallographic Association
